Subject: GCP Marketplace private offer — governance & drawdown cadence

Hi Morgan —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our call, I attached a draft commit schedule so we can align on how BlueHorizon will draw down the private offer. High level asks from Redwood for the governance cadence: 

- Monthly burn certification (simple one-pager) submitted by BlueHorizon finance.
- Escrow/release triggers: we propose a rolling 30-day buffer with a 1-month holdback that releases after consumption verification.
- Quarterly reconciliation (true-up) for co-sell credits and invoice alignment.
- Initial 30-day operational run followed by a monthly cadence once stable.

Attached: commit-schedule-draft.xlsx (tabbed by SKU + forecast).

Could you confirm: 1) who on your side will own the monthly cert (name/email), 2) whether legal needs an MSA amendment for escrow handling, and 3) whether BlueHorizon prefers the DocuSign or PDF route for the private offer acceptance?

If it helps, Marissa and Jonas are ready to run a quick 30-min ops sync tomorrow to walk the schedule and responsibilities.

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm owner for monthly cert by EOD Thu (9/9).
2) Legal to confirm escrow clause expectations (Alicia if involved).
3) Ops sync to finalize SLOs for the first 30-day run.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Marketplace Manager, Redwood Inference

Priyom —

Appreciate the clarity here and the spreadsheet. Quick answers:

1) Monthly cert owner: Me (Morgan Chen) with finance lead copying (finance@bluehorizon.ai).
2) Legal (Alicia) is looped for escrow language; BlueHorizon prefers an independent escrow agent if feasible.
3) DocuSign is preferred for signatures.

A few follow-ups from procurement side (attached):
- We need to understand who holds the escrow and what triggers a release (consumption report vs. invoice).
- What level of detail will Redwood require in the monthly cert? We prefer a short template rather than a ledger export.

Proposed cadence from our side: weekly short ops check for the first two weeks, then bi-weekly for month one, then monthly after that. Also asking whether Redwood can provide a one-page governance runbook we can include for our procurement folder.

I'll have Alicia send preferred redlines for escrow. Attach: procurement-questions.pdf (high level).

Thanks — Morgan

Morgan / team —

Thanks Morgan. To make this operationally light on both sides, Redwood proposes: 

- Monthly cert: one-page template (we've attached a v1 governance rules doc with the template tab). The cert should confirm total committed SKU burn in the prior month and any credits applied.
- Escrow: Redwood is open to using an independent escrow agent; proposal below: escrow holds the committed funds (or committed credit) and releases on a rolling 30-day verification window after monthly cert submission. This protects BlueHorizon for unused committed capacity while allowing Redwood predictable drawdown.
- Co-sell credits: credits will be tracked in HubSpot (link below) and applied as line-item adjustments on the monthly invoice; quarterly true-up for any discrepancies.

Suggested timeline:
- Wed 9/08: Ops sync (30 min) to align owners and cert template.
- 9/09: Legal to exchange redlines.
- 9/14: Finalize DocuSign packet for signature.

Link to HubSpot deal notes: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8421
Attached: governance-rules-v1.pdf (includes cert template).

Jonas will run the technical onboarding check in parallel and validate SKU mapping.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
